title: Tenant pausing profiles with KV-hinting and epoched fair queue
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem: Continuous batching increases GPU utilization but causes long-lived KV working sets and unfair tail latency for bursty tenants. Existing preemption mechanisms are coarse-grained (full-slice preempt) and evict KV without tenant signals, which either hurts latency for latency-sensitive tenants or causes excessive rebuild cost for large-model tenants.

Goal: Implement tenant-centric pausing profiles that define interruptibility and KV retention hints, and build an epoched fair-queueing layer which schedules micro-slices while respecting per-tenant SLO budgets and KV hint priorities. The feature should reduce median and p95 tail latency for high-priority tenants during contention, reduce KV rebuild churn for low-priority long-running slices, and keep overall throughput within 5% of baseline for steady workloads.

Scope: 1) a pausing profile API attached to tenant tokens (interruptible, soft-pause, non-interruptible) 2) KV hint metadata that tags cache entries with tenant, profile, and age_epoch 3) epoched fair queue that advances tenant epochs and grants micro-slice slots proportional to SLO-weighted budget 4) eviction backoff that uses hint priority and epoch hotness before full eviction 5) graceful fallback policies to lower-precision model variants if memory pressure is unresolved.

Why different: Instead of a pure time-slice preemptor or global KV-gc, this approach couples scheduling decisions with cache retention semantics to avoid the oscillation between evict/rebuild cycles. Epochs create logical windows that amortize KV rebuilds and enable predictable SLO accounting across bursts.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: model quantization changes, new GPU compaction kernels, or tenant billing changes.

Deliverables: design doc + concrete API, runtime scheduler code, KV metadata plumbing, integration tests (simulated multi-tenant traces), canary deployment config, dashboard panels (per-tenant epoch, eviction rate, rebuild cost).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements tenant pausing profiles with three modes and a configurable default
Epoched fair-queue grants micro-slice slots according to per-tenant SLO budgets and demonstrates stable fairness in a 50-tenant synthetic load test
KV entries are tagged with hint metadata and eviction backoff uses hint priority to reduce rebuild-to-evict ratio by >=35% on traced replay
Tail latency (p95) for SLO-sensitive tenants improves by >=25% under 2x baseline load compared to current baseline preemptor
End-to-end integration tests exist and run in CI; no increase in steady-state token cost >5%
Runbook and canary checklist added to runtime-ops playbook and Console shows new panels for epoch metrics
implementation_notes:
High-level plan: add pausing_profile field to tenant token metadata and extend request envelope. Scheduler: insert epoched queue between admission and batcher; an epoch advances when global slot counter passes a threshold or after fixed time quantum. Micro-slice: split large continuous batches into smaller interruptible micro-slices; each micro-slice carries pausing_profile. KV cache: store (tenant_id, profile, epoch, last_access_ts) metadata on entries; eviction chooses oldest epochs with lowest profile priority. Memory pressure hook: when GPU free memory < soft_watermark, trigger backoff that demotes interruptible micro-slices and applies graceful token-level pause rather than immediate eviction. Metrics: we will instrument eviction_reason, rebuild_time_ms, epoch_hit_rate, and per-tenant_slo_burn_rate.

Notes on migration: default profile for existing tenants = soft-pause. We'll progressively roll out by tenant cohorts: non-critical -> standard -> SLO-critical.
tradeoffs_decisions: Decision: use logical epochs (coarse-grained) not per-request counters to reduce metadata churn
Trade-off: micro-slices increase scheduling complexity and slightly increase context-switch overhead; chosen because they offer fine-grained fairness without full eviction frequency
Decision: tag KV entries with profile priority (3 levels) instead of weight floats to keep eviction fast in hot paths
Trade-off: delaying eviction may increase peak memory pressure; mitigated by fallback to lower-precision variants and immediate soft-preempt when below critical watermark
risks_mitigation: Risk: miscalibrated epochs could starve long-running high-throughput tenants. Mitigation: include safety bounds and a dynamic credit top-up if service-level deficit exceeds threshold
Risk: added metadata increases KV memory overhead. Mitigation: compress epoch/profile into a single 8-bit field and measure memory delta in perf tests
Risk: complexity in the hot path affects serving p99. Mitigation: put metadata checks behind optimized fast paths and benchmark with perf harness
